approved: Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Amendment (Dairy Cattle Export Charge) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a new statutory export charge on dairy cattle to fund research, development and marketing for the sector.
It would amend the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Act 1999 to allow a per head charge on dairy cattle exports, with a separate per kilogram rate for other cattle.
The charge would be set at $6 per head of dairy cattle exported, replacing a voluntary charge that was under-collected.
Imposes a statutory export charge on dairy cattle.
Sets the charge rate on a per head basis for dairy cattle.
Enables full funding of the Dairy Cattle Export Program.
Exporters of dairy cattle and the dairy cattle export sector.
Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Amendment (Dairy Cattle Export Charge) Bill 2020 - Second Reading - Against live export

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2020-09-03.184.1) to agree with the bill's main idea. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill for a [second time](https://peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/), which means they can now discuss it in more detail. ### What is the bill's main idea? According to the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd1920a/20bd103), the purpose of the bill is to: * *provide for the imposition of an export charge on the export of dairy cattle and* * *amend the rate provision to provide for two different rates of charges—a per head charge on dairy cattle and a per kilogram charge on cattle other than dairy cattle.*

The Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Amendment (Dairy Cattle Export Charge) Bill 2020 imposes a mandatory $6 per head charge on exported dairy cattle, replacing the current voluntary charge, to fund marketing and research and development through LiveCorp. The dairy cattle export industry is valued at over $200 million, with over 100,000 cattle exported in 2019 to markets including China, Indonesia, Pakistan and Japan.

The opposition supported the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Amendment (Dairy Cattle Export Charge) Bill 2020, but moved an amendment condemning the government for failing to develop a comprehensive plan to achieve the National Farmers’ Federation’s vision of a $100 billion agriculture industry by 2030, despite the Prime Minister’s promise at the Dubbo Bush Summit over a year ago. The speaker also noted that voluntary levy contributions had dropped from 92% in 2011 to 3% by 2019, and criticised the government for lacking an overarching strategic plan for agriculture, citing the Future Drought Fund as another example of headline numbers without follow-through.

The speaker advocated for a fairer farmgate milk price, extended eligibility for special disaster loans, and case managers for bushfire-affected farmers, and called for a national plan for the dairy industry. They noted a $5 million biogas plant turning manure into electricity and supported moving to zero net emissions by 2050.

The bill makes the Livestock Exporters' Council voluntary code mandatory and funds research and development for live cattle exports. The speaker noted a rise in dairy cattle exports due to drought and low prices, and called for further reforms including a mandatory code of conduct for the dairy industry and competition reform with divestment power.

The bill imposes a per-head export charge on dairy cattle to fund research, development, and marketing for the sector, replacing an undercollected voluntary charge. It was supported by a majority of licensed exporters and aims to improve animal welfare, market access, and regulatory performance for the $200 million dairy cattle export industry.
